review_notes: I read all of Model.lean (lines 1–116). The file has no @[simp] declarations of its own. I then checked how the other files in OAI/RepresentationTheory/Saxl use wordRep, rowWord, columnGroup, cyclic and polytabloid. The findings come from the repeated manual unfolding I found there. I did not check the exact simp normal form after each proposed change, and I did not run Lean. The proposed lemma statements are sketches that still need a compile check. I did not report simp annotations on canonicalTableau, kronecker or staircase; I found no concrete use that would benefit.

findings.excerpt: toFun := fun f a => f (a ∘ g)
findings.problem: The file gives no canonical simp lemma for how `wordRep n d g f` evaluates at a word. Downstream proofs instead unfold the definition and list the structure-coercion lemmas by hand. The same simp set `wordRep, MonoidHom.coe_mk, OneHom.coe_mk, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, Pi.single_apply` is repeated in Basic.lean `polytabloid_rowWord` and in HighProjection.lean `polytabloid_support`. SpechtSubmodule.lean `wordPair_move` uses `simpa [dotProduct, wordPerm, wordRep, ...]`. Several other places use `change` to see through `wordRep`. Unfolding `wordRep` through these coercions depends on the definition's internal structure, so it is brittle and not a stable normal form.
findings.proposed_change: Directly after `wordRep`, add `@[simp] lemma wordRep_apply (g : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (f : WordSpace n d) (a : Fin n → Fin d) : wordRep n d g f a = f (a ∘ g) := rfl`. Then replace the long `simp only [... wordRep, MonoidHom.coe_mk, ...]` calls with `simp only [wordRep_apply, ...]`. Also consider tagging `wordRep_single` (Polytabloid.lean:98) `@[simp]`. Its LHS is the unapplied `wordRep n d g (Pi.single a 1)`, so it does not compete with `wordRep_apply`. Many call sites currently invoke it by hand via `rw`, `simp_rw` or `simp only`. Only the `wordRep_apply` change is argued here with evidence.
findings.benefit: One orientation-stable rule, `wordRep g f a = f (a ∘ g)`, replaces ad hoc unfolding of the structure projections. This shortens proofs such as `polytabloid_rowWord` and `polytabloid_support`. It also keeps the proofs working if the internal construction of `wordRep` changes.

findings.problem: `columnGroup` has no membership characterization lemma, so simp cannot turn `g ∈ columnGroup t` into the pointwise column condition. Users instead rely on definitional unfolding. They write `have hc : g ∈ columnGroup tt := by intro i; exact ...`, or `change` to expose the condition (Polytabloid.lean `hcol` uses `intro i; change (t (f i)).val.2 = _; simp [f]`). They also extract the condition with `g.property i`. This is the usual case where a subgroup defined by a `carrier` set should come with a `mem_...` iff lemma.
findings.proposed_change: After the definition add `@[simp] lemma mem_columnGroup {n} {μ} (t : Tableau n μ) (g : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : g ∈ columnGroup t ↔ ∀ i, (t (g i)).val.2 = (t i).val.2 := Iff.rfl`. Then proofs of the form `intro i; change ...; simp` become `simp [mem_columnGroup]`. Uses of `g.property i` can become `(mem_columnGroup t _).1 g.property i`. Since the RHS contains no membership, there is no loop risk.
findings.benefit: `simp` and `rw` can reduce and prove column-group membership without depending on the definitional unfolding of the subgroup carrier. This removes the `change` and `intro` workarounds at several call sites and keeps the proofs readable.

findings.problem: `rowWord` is a plain def with no simp lemma for its coordinates, such as `(rowWord t i).val = (t i).val.1`. Because of this, many proofs unfold `rowWord` together with the specific tableau constructions around it. Examples are `simpa [rowWord, j, rowLetterInclusion, i]`, `simp only [... rowWord, stairRowTableau, rotateRowPositions, ...]` and `simpa [a, rowWord, stairRowTableau, ...]`. Unfolding the Fin-valued function exposes the anonymous-constructor term and its dependent proof, rather than the row index `(t i).val.1`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma rowWord_val {n μ} (t : Tableau n μ) (i : Fin n) : (rowWord t i).val = (t i).val.1 := rfl`. A plain `rowWord_apply : rowWord t i = ⟨_, _⟩` would carry a proof term and is worse. With `rowWord_val`, the call sites can replace `rowWord` in their simp lists with `rowWord_val`. The `Fin.val` form is what these proofs consume, for instance after `congrArg Fin.val (congrFun hh k)`.
findings.benefit: Callers get the row index directly, instead of unfolding `rowWord` and fighting the dependent proof term. They no longer need to list `rowWord` itself in simp sets that also unfold tableau constructions, so those simp calls are less likely to over-unfold. The statement `rowWord` is meant to expose, 'the row coordinate of the cell', becomes the simp normal form.
